name: Site utilities
notes: Pipe, hydrant and structure prices are anchored on DOT weighted-average bid prices (FDOT statewide Sep 2025-Aug 2026; ArDOT Jun 2025-Jun 2026; MDT 2025). DOT utility pipe items are usually utility relocations inside an active roadway (traffic control, conflicts, small runs), so they run at or above typical greenfield private-site main costs; methods account for this. On-site septic, wells, electrical primary/transformers, lift stations and utility pedestals had no authoritative public unit price available in this session and are derived; RV and food-truck pedestals reuse evidence collected by the RV park and food truck park type files.

items.name: Water main, 8" PVC C900 / DI (incl. fittings, valves amortized, trench & backfill)

cost.method: FDOT utility pipe PVC water/sewer 8" $115.60/LF (7 contracts, e1); FDOT ductile iron 8" $123.64/LF and 12" $117.08/LF (e2); ArDOT PVC C900 DR14 $117.50/LF on 10,700 LF (e3). Mid $115 = the cluster of all three DOT prices. Low $70 = long, unobstructed greenfield runs in low-cost markets (DOT relocation work carries a premium); high $175 = 12" DI / urban conditions with pavement restoration.

items.notes: On-site loop / private fire line. Gate valves ~every 500 ft and fittings are amortized in the LF price. Add fire-hydrant (ea) separately.

items.name: Sanitary sewer, 8" PVC gravity at 6-12' depth (incl. manholes ~every 350 ft)

cost.method: Pipe: FDOT PVC water/sewer 8" $115.60/LF (e1) as the in-trench pipe price. Manholes: FDOT manhole P-7/P-8 <10' $7,320-$8,295 each (e7) spread over ~350 LF = ~$22-$24/LF. Mid = $115 + $24 = ~$140. Low = shallow greenfield runs at ~$70/LF pipe + manholes; high = 12-18' depths with dewatering or rock.

items.notes: Services/laterals extra (~$1,500-$4,000 each). Deeper than ~14 ft or in rock: use the high end or add rock-excavation.

items.name: Storm sewer pipe, 18-24" RCP/HDPE in place (excl. inlets/manholes)

cost.method: FDOT pipe culvert, optional material, round 18" $121.00/LF (91 contracts, 133,261 LF) and 24" $135.99/LF (e5); ArDOT 18" RCP class 3 $91.21/LF and 24" $126.71/LF (e6). Mid $125 = average of the four; low = ArDOT 18" less private-site efficiency; high = 36" pipe (FDOT $208.05/LF).

items.notes: Add storm-inlet and manhole items for structures. Larger trunk lines: 30" ~$175, 36" ~$210, 48" ~$300/LF (FDOT).

items.name: Storm inlet / catch basin (curb or ditch-bottom, <10' deep)

cost.method: FDOT inlets: ditch-bottom type C <10' $6,518.82 (146 EA), type D $7,257.63 (204 EA), curb type P-5 $9,687.94 (207 EA), gutter type S $7,731.44 (391 EA) (e8). Mid $8,500 = central value of these high-volume items; low/high = shallow yard drains to J-bottom/deeper curb inlets ($14k-$15k).

items.notes: Parking lots typically need ~1 inlet per 10,000-20,000 SF of pavement.

items.name: Manhole, precast 4-5' dia, <10' deep (storm or sanitary)
items.notes: Sanitary manholes with drop connections or lining run at the high end.

items.name: Sewer force main, 4-6" PVC/HDPE (incl. air release allowance)

cost.method: FDOT utility pipe HDPE water/sewer 4" $68.41/LF and 6" $88.33/LF (e4); FDOT PVC 4" $102.30/LF (6 contracts, 518 LF, e1). Samples are small (relocation work), so mid $75 ~ midpoint of HDPE 4"-6"; low $40 = long open-cut rural runs; high $120 = directional-drilled or urban runs.

items.notes: Pair with lift-station. Directionally drilled HDPE is common under roads/wetlands.

items.name: Underground electrical primary (duct bank w/ 2-3 conduits, trench, cable allowance)

cost.method: FDOT conduit furnish & install, open trench $17.51/LF and directional bore $35.87/LF (e9) - single small conduit. A primary run typically needs 2-3 x 4-6" conduits (sometimes concrete-encased), deeper trench, warning tape and pull boxes/vaults (FDOT pull & splice boxes $1,476-$5,780 each), plus primary cable where the developer installs it: ~2.5-4x a single-conduit price -> $50-$150/LF; mid $85. In many utility territories the utility installs cable and the developer only trenches/installs conduit (use the low end).

items.notes: Utility line-extension charges/aid-in-construction vary widely by utility and are not included; treat them as a fee or off-site item.

items.name: Transformer pad & connections (utility-furnished pad-mount transformer)

cost.method: Derived (no public unit price captured). Developer scope when the utility furnishes and sets the transformer: precast or cast-in-place pad/box pad ($2k-$8k), grounding grid, bollards ($1k-$3k), primary and secondary conduit stub-ups ($2k-$10k) and secondary feeders to the building service (short runs). Mid $15k for a single 3-phase commercial service; high $40k for large services with long secondary runs.

items.notes: If the owner must purchase the transformer (campus/private distribution, some solar/EV sites), use transformer-owner-furnished instead/in addition.

items.name: Pad-mount transformer, owner-furnished & installed (≈300-750 kVA, 3-phase)

cost.method: Derived (no public price list available). Distribution-transformer prices rose sharply after 2020 with long lead times; a 300-750 kVA 3-phase pad-mount unit is assumed at ~$35k-$140k equipment plus $10k-$40k pad, rigging, terminations and testing. Mid $85k for ~500 kVA. Verify with a current supplier quote - lead times of 1-2+ years can drive premiums.

items.notes: Optional item; most single-building commercial services use a utility-owned transformer (transformer-pad).

items.name: Sewage lift station, packaged duplex submersible (wet well, pumps, controls, generator receptacle)

cost.method: FDOT 12-month average shows one public sanitary lift station at $497,334 (e10, single contract - municipal spec). Private-development packaged duplex stations (100-300 gpm) commonly run well below municipal stations; small private stations without standby generator ~$150k. Mid $350k reflects a developer station built to utility-dedication standards (precast wet well, valve vault, duplex submersibles, control panel, telemetry, fencing, access drive). High $750k = larger station with on-site generator and odor control.

items.notes: Grinder-pump systems for very small flows can be $15k-$40k instead. Add force-main LF separately.

items.name: Fire hydrant assembly (hydrant, tee, gate valve, lead)

cost.method: FDOT fire hydrant F&I standard $10,255.96 (14 EA), 3-way $9,768.38 (21 EA), 2-hose $14,400 (1 EA) (e11); ArDOT fire hydrant assembly $10,665.93 (27 EA) (e12); MDT hydrant assembly $14,600 (2 EA) (e13). Mid $11,000 = weighted center of FDOT/ArDOT; high = MDT/FDOT single-contract prices; low = greenfield sites with short leads.

items.notes: Typical spacing 300-500 ft on site loops; fire code driven.

items.name: Off-site utility extension in public ROW (water + sewer in common corridor, incl. pavement restoration)

cost.method: Per LF of corridor carrying both an 8" water main (~$115/LF, e1) and 8" gravity sewer with manholes (~$140/LF, e1/e7), plus trench pavement cut-and-patch and traffic control in public ROW (~$60-$150/LF using HMA at FDOT $136/ton), plus valves/connections and inspection by the utility -> ~$315-$405; mid $375. Low $200 = single utility along an unpaved shoulder; high $650 = urban street with full-lane restoration, deeper sewer or bores.

items.notes: Off-site; excluded from the baseline hard cost by definition and added only when the user switches it on. Reimbursement/latecomer agreements may offset cost.

items.name: Septic system, conventional (≈1,000-1,500 gal tank + gravity drainfield; small building)

cost.method: Derived; no authoritative public source was retrievable in this session (consumer cost sites blocked automated access). Conventional systems for a single home/small building are widely quoted at ~$5k-$15k in prior years; for a small commercial building (higher design flow, engineered design, commercial permit, effluent filter, heavier tank) assumed 1.5-2.5x -> $10k-$40k, mid $20k. Mound/aerobic/ATU systems sit at the high end.

items.notes: For larger flows (campgrounds, multiple buildings) use drainfield-large. Perc testing/design are soft costs.

items.name: Large on-site wastewater system (≈2,000-10,000 gpd; tanks, dosing/LPP drainfield)

cost.method: Anchor: an RV park developer source reports small parks doing their 'entire septic for $100k' (rv-park-resort.json#e14, low confidence). Scaled by design flow: ~$15-$35 per gpd of design flow for multiple tanks, dosing pumps/controls and pressure-distribution field -> 4,000-10,000 gpd = $60k-$350k; mid $150k (~6,000 gpd). Package treatment plants (>$1M) are not included.

items.notes: Large-capacity septic systems often need state (not county) permits and EPA UIC registration.

items.name: Water well, drilled (≈300-600 ft) with pump, pitless adapter, pressure tank - small non-community system

cost.method: Derived (no retrievable public source this session). Drilling at ~$30-$90/LF for 6" wells x 300-600 ft = $9k-$54k, plus submersible pump, pitless adapter, pressure tanks and controls $6k-$20k, plus disinfection/testing; public-water-system (non-community) wells add grouting, wellhouse and treatment allowances -> $20k-$120k, mid $45k.

items.notes: Storage tanks, treatment and fire-flow systems are extra. Highly variable with depth and geology.

items.name: RV site utility pedestal, 50/30/20A (installed, incl. share of site feeder)

cost.method: Pedestal hardware ~$500-$600 each (city council estimate, rv-park-resort.json#e13); an RV park developer source puts electrical at ~$4,000 per site including distribution (rv-park-resort.json#e9). Installed pedestal (setting, breakers, metering option, short secondary from the loop) assumed ~$1.5k-$3k; mid $3,000 includes a partial share of feeders. Use high $5,500 when each pedestal also carries metering and long trench runs. Water/sewer hookups are separate.

items.notes: Matches the RV park type file's electrical-pedestal line item ($1,200-$3,500). Does not include transformer/service equipment.

items.name: Food truck pad utility pedestal (≈50-100A power, water & sewer/grey-water stub)

cost.method: A Utah special service district estimate lists 'Electrical For Food Truck 1 LS 10,000.00' per truck pad (food-truck-park.json#e5) - used as the mid. Low $5k = power-only pedestal near the service; high $20k = 100A service plus potable water, grey-water/sewer stub and backflow per pad.

items.notes: Per truck position. Grease interceptor and restrooms are carried in the food truck park type file.
